title: Modern Masters
description: The turn into modernism — symbolism and expression at the dawn of the new century.
source: Art Institute of Chicago, Wikimedia Commons

items.title: Paris Street; Rainy Day
items.description_narrative: Gustave Caillebotte's 'Paris Street; Rainy Day' captures a striking urban scene in 1877 Paris, depicting well-dressed figures strolling under umbrellas on a wet street. The composition offers a unique perspective of modern city life, characterized by its precise realism and distinctive viewpoints.
items.tags: urban life, street scene, rainy day, 19th century, realism, city, umbrellas, french art

items.title: Hercules and the Lernaean Hydra
items.description_narrative: Gustave Moreau's 'Hercules and the Lernaean Hydra' dramatically depicts the heroic figure surveying the slain multi-headed monster amid a landscape strewn with its victims. This powerful work exemplifies Moreau's Symbolist approach, rich with intricate details and a somber, mythical atmosphere.
items.tags: mythology, symbolism, hercules, hydra, french, heroic, dramatic, oil painting

items.title: Calf's Head and Ox Tongue
items.description_narrative: This painting presents a starkly realistic still life featuring a butchered calf's head and an ox tongue, rendered with unflinching detail. Gustave Caillebotte's meticulous brushwork captures the textures and forms of the meat, reflecting his mastery of realistic depiction.
items.tags: still life, realism, meat, food, detailed, oil painting, 19th century

items.title: Alpine Scene
items.description_narrative: Gustave Doré's 'Alpine Scene' from 1865 captures the majestic beauty of mountainous landscapes through oil on canvas. This painting exemplifies his ability to render dramatic natural environments with intricate detail and atmospheric depth.
items.tags: landscape, alpine, mountains, oil painting, 19th century, romanticism, french, sublime

items.title: Mère Grégoire
items.description_narrative: Gustave Courbet's 'Mère Grégoire' is an oil on canvas portrait depicting an older woman. This work exemplifies Courbet's commitment to portraying everyday people with directness and realism.
items.tags: portrait, woman, realism, french realism, direct, naturalistic, oil painting

items.title: The Rock of Hautepierre
items.description_narrative: Gustave Courbet's 'The Rock of Hautepierre' depicts a rugged natural landscape with a prominent rock formation. This oil on canvas exemplifies Courbet's commitment to Realism, capturing the unadorned beauty of the natural world.
items.tags: landscape, realism, nature, oil painting, rock formation, french art

items.title: An Alpine Scene
items.description_narrative: Gustave Courbet's "An Alpine Scene" captures a dramatic mountain landscape, rendered with the artist's characteristic impasto technique. This oil on canvas work from 1874 exemplifies his dedication to depicting natural subjects with unflinching realism.
items.tags: landscape, Realism, oil painting, French art, mountain, nature, alpine, Courbet

items.title: The Valley of Les Puits-Noir
items.description_narrative: Gustave Courbet's 'The Valley of Les Puits-Noir' depicts a rugged, unidealized landscape from his native Jura region in eastern France. Executed in oil on canvas, this work exemplifies his Realist approach, capturing nature with a somber palette and textured brushwork.
items.tags: landscape, realism, french art, 19th century, nature, valley, oil painting

items.title: Rêverie (Portrait of Gabrielle Borreau)
items.medium: Oil on paper, mounted on canvas
items.description_narrative: This intimate portrait by Gustave Courbet depicts Gabrielle Borreau in a contemplative pose. Painted in 1862, the work captures a moment of quiet introspection.
items.tags: portrait, realism, 19th century, contemplative, figure study, oil painting, french art

items.title: Cliffs on the Sea Coast: Small Beach, Sunrise (Falaise au bord de la mer, vu Petite Plage, soleil levant)
items.description_narrative: Gustave Courbet captures the rugged beauty of a coastal scene in 'Cliffs on the Sea Coast: Small Beach, Sunrise.' This oil on canvas painting from 1865 depicts a dramatic interplay of light and shadow on the cliffs as the sun rises over the sea.
items.tags: seascape, landscape, realism, nature, cliffs, sunrise, oil painting

items.title: The Brook of Les Puits-Noir
items.description_narrative: Gustave Courbet captures the quiet solitude of a brook winding through a densely wooded landscape in Les Puits-Noir. This painting exemplifies his commitment to depicting unidealized nature with a robust, earthy palette.
items.tags: landscape, nature, brook, forest, realism, 19th-century art, tranquil

items.title: The Girl by the Window
items.description_narrative: Edvard Munch's The Girl by the Window captures a moment of introspection and quiet solitude. This work exemplifies the artist's exploration of psychological states through the depiction of figures in evocative settings.
items.tags: expressionism, symbolism, psychological, solitude, figure painting, norwegian art, fin de siècle

items.title: The Kiss
items.medium: Oil and gold leaf on canvas
items.description_narrative: A couple locked in an intimate embrace, cloaked in elaborate gold-patterned robes, kneeling in a flower-strewn meadow. Klimt's masterful use of gold leaf and ornamental motifs epitomizes his 'Golden Phase' and the height of the Vienna Secession movement.
items.tags: love, gold, art nouveau, couple, embrace, ornamental

items.title: The Scream
items.medium: Oil, tempera, pastel and crayon on cardboard
items.description_narrative: An agonized figure against a tumultuous orange sky, standing on a bridge. Widely interpreted as representing the universal anxiety of modern humanity. Munch described the inspiration as feeling an infinite scream passing through nature.
items.tags: scream, anxiety, expressionism, bridge, sunset, anguish

items.title: Portrait of Jeanne Hébuterne
items.description_narrative: Modigliani portrays his companion and muse with his signature elongated neck, almond-shaped blank eyes, and tilted oval head against a flat, warm-toned ground. The portrait exemplifies his fusion of African sculptural form with Italian Renaissance portrait tradition.
items.tags: school of paris, portraiture, elongation, muse, modernism, montparnasse

items.title: Portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer I
items.medium: Oil, silver, and gold on canvas
items.description_narrative: Klimt envelops Viennese patron Adele Bloch-Bauer in shimmering, mosaic-like gold ornament, fusing Byzantine influence with Art Nouveau glamour. Later dubbed the "Woman in Gold" after a landmark restitution case, it remains Klimt's most celebrated portrait.
items.tags: vienna secession, gold leaf, portraiture, art nouveau, byzantine, symbolism

items.title: Bathers at Asnières
items.description_narrative: Working-class Parisians lounge and swim along the Seine at Asnières, bathed in flat, hazy summer light and rendered with Seurat's early experiments in broken brushwork. It was the artist's first large-scale Salon submission and a precursor to his masterpiece "A Sunday on La Grande Jatte."
items.tags: neo-impressionism, seine, leisure, pointillism precursor, national gallery london, working class

items.title: At the Moulin Rouge
items.description_narrative: Toulouse-Lautrec crowds a nocturnal cabaret table with sharply characterized Montmartre regulars, their faces lit by an eerie greenish glow while a ghostly woman looms in the foreground. Painted from the artist's intimate knowledge of the venue, it captures fin-de-siècle Paris at its most theatrical.
items.tags: montmartre, cabaret, nightlife, parisian bohemia, post-impressionism, art institute chicago

items.title: The Sick Child
items.description_narrative: Munch reworked this haunting image of a dying girl and her grieving mother throughout his career, scraping and repainting the canvas to evoke raw memory rather than polished illusion. Rooted in the death of his own sister, it announced the emotionally charged style that would culminate in "The Scream."
items.tags: symbolism, grief, illness, norwegian art, expressionism, memory

items.title: Judith I
items.description_narrative: Klimt recasts the biblical heroine Judith as a rapturous, half-undressed femme fatale cradling the severed head of Holofernes against a shimmering gold-leaf ground. The painting inaugurated the celebrated 'golden phase' of his career.

items.title: Jeanne Hébuterne with Yellow Sweater
items.description_narrative: Modigliani's companion Jeanne sits in a yellow sweater, her swanlike neck, tilted head and blank almond eyes pared down to pure, elegant contour. It was painted in the final months before the artist's death in 1920.

items.title: The Buddha
items.description_narrative: A robed Buddha stands in profile beside a flowering tree amid shimmering, jewel-toned fields of color. The work belongs to Redon's luminous late period, a mystical turn away from the somber charcoal 'noirs' of his earlier years.

items.title: Woman in a Striped Dress
items.description_narrative: A woman arranging flowers nearly dissolves into a dense weave of stripes, blossoms and patterned interior. One of a set of decorative panels made for the Natanson family, it embodies the intimate, flattened aesthetic of the Nabis.

items.title: The Sleeping Gypsy
items.description_narrative: A lion sniffs a sleeping mandolin-player beside her water jug under a full moon in a silent moonlit desert. Rousseau's most hauntingly still, dreamlike scene, it was later revered by the Surrealists.
items.tags: dream, lion, desert, moonlight, naive art, surreal

items.title: Woman on Rose Divan
items.cultural_context: Early French modernism, Matisse's Nice period
items.description_narrative: Painted during Matisse's years in Nice, this work belongs to a series of odalisque-inspired interiors in which he posed models amid richly patterned, decorative settings drenched in Mediterranean light. The reclining figure and ornamental surroundings reflect Matisse's enduring interest in pattern, color, and the sensuous pleasures of painting.

items.title: Landscape: Window Overlooking the Woods
items.cultural_context: Early French modernism, the Nabis group
items.description_narrative: Édouard Vuillard, a member of the Nabis, a group of young painters influenced by Paul Gauguin and Japanese prints, painted this densely patterned view through a window using flattened space and decorative surface texture. The Nabis rejected illusionistic depth in favor of paintings that asserted their own flat, patterned reality.

items.title: Te burao (The Hibiscus Tree)
items.description_narrative: Gauguin painted this scene of Tahitian women in the shade of a hibiscus tree during his first stay on the island, using flattened planes of saturated color and simplified forms drawn from his idealized vision of Polynesian life. Works like this, made in deliberate rejection of European academic convention, became a touchstone for early twentieth-century modernists searching for new visual languages.

items.title: No te aha oe riri (Why Are You Angry?)
items.description_narrative: Painted during Gauguin's second stay in Tahiti, this large canvas depicts a domestic dispute among Tahitian women rendered in bold, flattened color and a frieze-like arrangement of figures. Gauguin gave the painting a Tahitian title inscribed directly on the canvas, part of his deliberate effort to distance his work from European artistic tradition.

items.title: Sawmill, Outskirts of Paris
items.cultural_context: Early French modernism, self-taught Naive painting
items.description_narrative: Henri Rousseau, a self-taught toll collector who painted only on evenings and weekends, depicted this suburban sawmill on the edge of Paris with the flattened perspective and meticulous, almost obsessive detail that became his signature style. Rousseau's untrained but intensely personal vision was later championed by Picasso and other early modernists as a radical alternative to academic realism.

items.title: Mill of Pont Maupuit
items.cultural_context: Late Impressionism, color experiments anticipating Fauvism
items.description_narrative: Armand Guillaumin, a close friend of Cézanne and Pissarro who exhibited in several Impressionist group shows, painted this rural mill scene using the intensified, high-keyed color of his later career. His bold use of pure, saturated pigment in his final decades anticipated the color experiments of the Fauve painters who emerged in the years that followed.
